# Operator configuration

<!-- Generated by sdo/operator/cmd/configdoc from contracts/settings; do not edit. Run scripts/gen_config_docs.sh. -->

Operator configuration is how long SDO waits and how it responds. App memory (`.sdo/`) decides what counts as broken;
nothing here changes what an accepted detector decides.

## Setting it

`sdo-operator host` and `sdo-operator install-existing` resolve one configuration, in this order (later wins):

1. the defaults in this file;
2. each `--config FILE` (YAML, repeatable, applied in order; an unknown key is an error);
3. `SDO_<SECTION>_<KEY>` environment variables, derived from the YAML key path (the top-level `mode` is `SDO_MODE`).
   A list or an object is JSON. A variable that starts with a section prefix but names no key is an error.

No knob has a command-line flag of its own; the flags of `host` and `install-existing` name only the installation
(repository, namespaces, images, Secrets, PVC, registry, source and plan, agent registrations, run bounds) and, for `host`, the
inputs the people running the application give (`--goal`/`--goal-file`, `--journeys`/`--journeys-file`).

The installer writes the resolved result to the `sdo-config` ConfigMap, mounted read-only at `/etc/sdo/config.yaml` in the
operate and controller Jobs, which refuse to start without it; no policy value crosses their command lines. The controller
records the file under `.sdo-runtime/config.yaml` at start, its compiled child and its deployment health checks read that
record, and the evidence sink carries it to the run directory.

A value is read once, when a process starts; there is no hot reload. The ConfigMap's hash is part of the controller's
install fingerprint, so running `install-existing` again with a changed configuration replaces the running controller
(one way: the new values apply only through that replacement).

`sdo-operator config print [--config FILE]...` prints the resolved YAML.

For one release, `host` and `install-existing` refuse to start while `SDO_CODE_PATH` or `SDO_RESPONDER_MENU` is set in their
environment; use `SDO_AGENT_CODE_PATH` and `SDO_RESPONSE_MENU`.

## Benchmark profile

`benchmarks/fuzzops/sdo-bench.yaml` is the profile every benchmark harness passes first. It sets only what differs from the
defaults above: `response.repair_policy: recorded-actions`, `detection.self_heal_hold: 60s`, and, to measure the upper bound of what
learned playbooks achieve alone, `response.after_playbook: wait` with `response.after_playbook_wait: 5m`: after a playbook applied,
the agent is never dispatched; recovery gets the whole bound (slow readiness and windowed detectors need more than the
stage's default 90 seconds), then the incident escalates. Production keeps `agent`. It also names `agent.recording: false`
(the production default, written out so an experiment can set it to `true`): the agent-cluster recording is off, and a few runs
that show nothing missing without it are the case for removing it. It sets `onboarding.journeys_required: false`: a benchmark app has no people to give journeys, so
the onboarding agent discovers them (production requires them; a harness that has them passes `host --journeys`).

## Keys

### Top level

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `SDO_MODE` | enum | `operate` | how incidents are handled: operate (respond and learn), frozen (respond, learn nothing), watch-only (detect and verify, never respond) or external (external alerts only, close on responder completion) |

### `agent`

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent.provider` | `SDO_AGENT_PROVIDER` | string | `codex` | agent provider of every worker: codex or claude |
| `agent.model` | `SDO_AGENT_MODEL` | string | `""` | agent model of every worker (required) |
| `agent.effort` | `SDO_AGENT_EFFORT` | string | `medium` | reasoning effort of every worker: low, medium, high, xhigh or max |
| `agent.reasoning_summary` | `SDO_AGENT_REASONING_SUMMARY` | string | `auto` | reasoning summaries Codex workers record in their rollouts: auto, concise, detailed or none (auto and concise record readable summaries) |
| `agent.lifecycle_timeout` | `SDO_AGENT_LIFECYCLE_TIMEOUT` | duration | `1h0m0s` | limit of one lifecycle (detection designer) session |
| `agent.memory_check_timeout` | `SDO_AGENT_MEMORY_CHECK_TIMEOUT` | duration | `5m0s` | limit of one memory check a worker runs on its checkout |
| `agent.code_path` | `SDO_AGENT_CODE_PATH` | string | `go` | programming-model plugin set: go or shell |
| `agent.code_path_overrides` | `SDO_AGENT_CODE_PATH_OVERRIDES` | string | `""` | CodePathOverrides as a JSON object (for example {"response_stages":["agent"]}); empty selects the code path's own seams |
| `agent.recording` | `SDO_AGENT_RECORDING` | bool | `false` | whether the proxy every agent Kubernetes call goes through records those calls (the agent-cluster recording that memory.AgentWrites reads). Off by default and a candidate for removal: with it off the proxy still forwards, forces the responder field manager and applies the incident mutation fence, but keeps no history, so Recovered is timed from SDO's own plan writes and the controller's observed settle, the closing turn carries no recorded-changes list and learns on any success closure, and an exec or raw write by the agent moves no clock |
| `agent.extra_env` | `SDO_AGENT_EXTRA_ENV` | list (JSON) | `[]` | extra NAME=VALUE environment of every agent worker the controller launches (responders, standby, reflection and closing turn, health refresh, lifecycle agents) |

### `response`

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `response.timeout` | `SDO_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT` | duration | `30m0s` | how long the responder may work on one incident; the reflection deadline derives from it |
| `response.verification_timeout` | `SDO_RESPONSE_VERIFICATION_TIMEOUT` | duration | `5m0s` | how long the independent verification of a repair may take |
| `response.max_loops` | `SDO_RESPONSE_MAX_LOOPS` | int | `10` | mitigation rounds the responder agent may use per incident (the automatic stage's one apply does not count) |
| `response.diagnosis_deadline` | `SDO_RESPONSE_DIAGNOSIS_DEADLINE` | duration | `10s` | shared deadline of candidate diagnosis in the automatic stage |
| `response.stage_budget` | `SDO_RESPONSE_STAGE_BUDGET` | duration | `45s` | scheduling bound of one automatic-stage pass; a follow-up pass before responder handoff may take up to twice this |
| `response.repair_policy` | `SDO_RESPONSE_REPAIR_POLICY` | string | `commit` | the evidence the controller requires for a responder repair: commit (a source repair is committed through the broker; production) or recorded-actions (live cluster repairs are recorded as actions without a source commit; benchmark runs) |
| `response.after_playbook` | `SDO_RESPONSE_AFTER_PLAYBOOK` | string | `agent` | what happens when a learned playbook applied and the alert set did not recover within the stage's bound: agent (dispatch the agent, told what the playbook did), escalate (no agent; the incident stays open under ordinary closure and closes failed at the verification timeout if the alerts never clear) or wait (keep waiting for recovery up to after_playbook_wait, then escalate). When recovery holds, no agent runs in any setting; recovery is judged on the incident's whole alert set (opening alerts plus joined user tests), so a joined test still failing at the bound dispatches the agent |
| `response.after_playbook_wait` | `SDO_RESPONSE_AFTER_PLAYBOOK_WAIT` | duration | `5m0s` | how long after_playbook: wait keeps waiting for the alert set to recover after the playbook applied, capped by the response timeout; under agent and escalate it caps the estimated wait after the playbook's last write |
| `response.dispatch_prepare_bound` | `SDO_RESPONSE_DISPATCH_PREPARE_BOUND` | duration | `2m0s` | how long a transient failure to prepare the responder's task (a Git, IO or Kubernetes API error) is retried with backoff before the incident escalates without an agent, capped by the response timeout; a permanent failure (unreadable operational memory, a task over budget) escalates at once |
| `response.standby` | `SDO_RESPONSE_STANDBY` | bool | `true` | pre-start a responder worker; false forces cold Jobs |
| `response.menu` | `SDO_RESPONSE_MENU` | bool | `true` | offer the responder its tool menu |
| `response.builtin_restore_auto` | `SDO_RESPONSE_BUILTIN_RESTORE_AUTO` | bool | `false` | let the automatic stage apply the built-in source-restore playbook (put a component's non-SDO departures from accepted source back) when its diagnosis matches; off, it is only offered like any playbook and the responder decides |
| `response.permissive` | `SDO_RESPONSE_PERMISSIVE` | bool | `false` | broad lane repair permissions excluding Secret and credential APIs |
| `response.permissive_namespaces` | `SDO_RESPONSE_PERMISSIVE_NAMESPACES` | list (JSON) | `[]` | additional lane namespaces the permissive responder may repair |
| `response.cleanup_turns` | `SDO_RESPONSE_CLEANUP_TURNS` | int | `2` | how many times the responder's session is asked, after Recovered, to keep or remove the app-file edits it left uncaptured; edits still left after that are discarded and recorded as source_repair_uncaptured. 0 asks no cleanup turn |
| `response.page_only` | `SDO_RESPONSE_PAGE_ONLY` | bool | `false` | the responder is a plain agent that gets only the incident page: no sdo commands on its PATH, no skills, no memory checkout, no investigators, no closing or cleanup turn, and no learning from the incident. SDO still detects, pages and verifies as usual. For comparing SDO's page alone against SDO's tools and memory |
| `response.external_clues` | `SDO_RESPONSE_EXTERNAL_CLUES` | bool | `false` | with mode external: keep the detectors, synthetic traffic and state baseline running as clues (sdo detect, the candidate view). Their findings never open, join or close an external incident; the caller opens it and the responder's completion closes it. Default off: an external controller observes nothing |
| `response.investigators` | `SDO_RESPONSE_INVESTIGATORS` | int | `0` | how many read-only investigator sessions SDO starts when the responder has made no write for investigator_delay: one per top candidate node with non-routine evidence, each testing one hypothesis and writing a report the responder reads with sdo investigations. They never fix, never close or escalate an incident and are stopped before the closing turn. 0 starts none |
| `response.investigator_delay` | `SDO_RESPONSE_INVESTIGATOR_DELAY` | duration | `1m0s` | how long the responder may work without a write before investigators start; a fix faster than this costs nothing. Measured fast fixes land in 25-60 s, so the 60s default starts them only for the slow incidents |
| `response.startup_bound` | `SDO_RESPONSE_STARTUP_BOUND` | duration | `30m0s` | how long a new install waits for SDO to see its application healthy (2 min with no opener firing) before detectors can open incidents. Pages can start the responder during startup. 0s turns the start-up period off |

### `detection`

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `detection.self_heal_hold` | `SDO_DETECTION_SELF_HEAL_HOLD` | duration | `5m0s` | how long a Kubernetes condition without a give-up signal must hold before it opens an incident; carried in every detector observation and bound into the operability report |
| `detection.stability_window` | `SDO_DETECTION_STABILITY_WINDOW` | duration | `15s` | how long the alert set (opening alerts and user tests that failed during the incident) must stay clear after SDO's last write settled before the incident counts as recovered |
| `detection.drift_batch_window` | `SDO_DETECTION_DRIFT_BATCH_WINDOW` | duration | `20s` | batch window for unexplained drift |
| `detection.request_metrics_shadow` | `SDO_DETECTION_REQUEST_METRICS_SHADOW` | bool | `false` | shadow mode of the request-metrics detector: its per-operation findings are recorded as clues in sdo detect and the evidence sink but never open or hold an incident. Off by default: a failing operation or route in real user traffic opens an incident |

### `learning`

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `learning.replay` | `SDO_LEARNING_REPLAY` | string | `on` | replay and corpus capture: on or off |
| `learning.reflection_guidance` | `SDO_LEARNING_REFLECTION_GUIDANCE` | string | `baseline` | the agent's learning instructions: baseline learns from each confirmed cause; generalize compares related incident signatures and parameterizes a shared playbook; generalize-spec favors predicates visible in resource spec or status. None changes the detector SDK or the validator |
| `learning.force_reflection` | `SDO_LEARNING_FORCE_REFLECTION` | bool | `false` | always dispatch reflection after a verified closure (not with a frozen mode) |
| `learning.closing_turn` | `SDO_LEARNING_CLOSING_TURN` | bool | `true` | whether a closed incident is learned from: the responder session's closing turn and cleanup turns, and Go's corpus capture. Off: detection, response, verification and the committed outcome are unchanged, but the incident's work ends when its outcome is acknowledged and nothing is learned (the ledger's reflection_skipped_reason is closing_turn_off); a committed source repair is still deployed. For runs whose learning is discarded (a benchmark arm that measures a fixed memory) |
| `learning.healthy_baseline` | `SDO_LEARNING_HEALTHY_BASELINE` | bool | `false` | opt-in detector gate: a proposal that changes learned detector source is replayed against healthy snapshots a runner recorded with sdo-operator baseline-write (one sdktest.Snapshot JSON per file, outside the accepted repository); a detector that fires on one fails validation, and a missing baseline fails closed. It never reads benchmark verdicts |

### `deployment`

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deployment.max_attempts` | `SDO_DEPLOYMENT_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | int | `3` | maximum deployment attempts |
| `deployment.build_timeout` | `SDO_DEPLOYMENT_BUILD_TIMEOUT` | duration | `30m0s` | deadline of one source image build |
| `deployment.build_budget` | `SDO_DEPLOYMENT_BUILD_BUDGET` | duration | `1h0m0s` | deadline of all source image builds of one deployment attempt |
| `deployment.rollout_timeout` | `SDO_DEPLOYMENT_ROLLOUT_TIMEOUT` | duration | `10m0s` | how long to wait for each applied workload to finish rolling out |
| `deployment.policy` | `SDO_DEPLOYMENT_POLICY` | object (JSON) | `{}` | install-time deployment policy as a JSON object (registry allowlist, scope blocking and grants) |

### `evidence`

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `evidence.host_path` | `SDO_EVIDENCE_HOST_PATH` | string | `""` | node directory that receives run evidence (writable by uid 65532); outlives the control namespace |
| `evidence.volume` | `SDO_EVIDENCE_VOLUME` | string | `""` | evidence sink as a Kubernetes VolumeSource JSON; excludes host_path |
| `evidence.run_id` | `SDO_EVIDENCE_RUN_ID` | string | `""` | run directory inside the evidence sink (empty: the control namespace) |

### `telemetry`

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `telemetry.profile` | `SDO_TELEMETRY_PROFILE` | string | `prometheus-default` | application telemetry profile: a built-in name (prometheus-default, none), a YAML or JSON file, or an inline JSON document |
| `telemetry.sources` | `SDO_TELEMETRY_SOURCES` | list (JSON) | `[]` | operator-provided external Prometheus-compatible metrics sources as ID=URL; the first becomes the default when the profile has none |

### `source`

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `source.poll_interval` | `SDO_SOURCE_POLL_INTERVAL` | duration | `30s` | how often the controller looks for a branch head SDO did not write (an engineer's push), to deploy and verify it |

### `onboarding`

| Key | Env | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `onboarding.journeys_required` | `SDO_ONBOARDING_JOURNEYS_REQUIRED` | bool | `true` | whether onboarding requires the user journeys SDO must support, given by the people running the application as free text (host --journeys or --journeys-file, or a journeys: list in the goal file's front matter). On, a host or operate launch without them stops before any agent runs; off, the onboarding agent discovers the journeys itself |
| `onboarding.soak` | `SDO_ONBOARDING_SOAK` | duration | `5m0s` | how long a new install's controller runs the committed probes on their schedule, once every opener detector has been evaluated, before its start-up period can end: the onboarding healthy run, judged like onboarding journeys --soak and recorded once per install in the sdo-onboarding-soak ConfigMap. Its reds never open an incident; sdo-operator onboarding soak reads the record and, when red, prints the one follow-up turn for the onboarding session. 0s soaks nothing |

## App-memory defaults

These are not operator configuration. Each is authored per detector or probe in app memory; the SDK constant is the
fallback when a field is left unset.

| Value | Fallback | Source |
|---|---|---|
| probe health minimum duration | `9s` | `traffic.DefaultHealthMinDuration` |
| probe SLO window (samples) | `5` | `traffic.DefaultWindow` |
| probe SLO minimum samples | `3` | `traffic.DefaultMinSamples` |
| probe SLO maximum sample age | `30s` | `traffic.DefaultMaxAge` |
| probe SLO maximum error rate | `0.5` | `traffic.DefaultMaxErrorRate` |
| probe SLO maximum timeout rate | `0.5` | `traffic.DefaultMaxTimeoutRate` |
| probe SLO maximum latency | `1.5s` | `traffic.DefaultMaxLatency` |

## Internal worker variables

These are written by the controller into worker Jobs, or read by `sdo-operator memory check` inside workers. They are
transport, not knobs, and keep their names.

- `SDO_AGENT_GUIDANCE`
- `SDO_DEPLOYMENT_MODEL`
- `SDO_TELEMETRY_POLICY`
- `SDO_AGENT_SCRIPT_*`
- `SDO_TASK_PATH`
- `SDO_INCIDENT_ID`
- `SDO_REPLAY`
- `SDO_CODE_PATH`
- `SDO_LIFECYCLE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`
- `SDO_MEMORY_CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`
- `SDO_RESPONDER_MODEL`
- `SDO_REFLECTION_MODEL`
- `SDO_LIFECYCLE_MODEL`
